Fair point; I took calc once upon a time myself, although I have to admit when he talks of how important some of those algorithms are I've no real sense of why that truly is.

By themselves, they aren't really useful. What they can do, however, is give insight as to do other things, how to discover or write new algorithms, or how to predict complexity. By themselves, they don't really do much. The thinking is that portions of them can be used directly or for inspiration into new methods.

The term is actually new to me. It's newer than my time in academia, I do believe.

It reminds me a bit of Russell's proof that 1 + 1 = 2, in Principia Mathematica. That took him a couple of hundred pages of pure math and a little bit of English.
